items.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
items.summary: In the tiny nation, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

items.title: Heat Is Hammering Europe, Again. Here’s What That Looks Like.
items.summary: Extreme temperatures and repeated wildfires are pushing infrastructure to the limit and testing the continent’s resolve.

items.title: The Taliban Kicked the U.S. Out of Afghanistan. Now They Want It Back.
items.summary: In an interview, Afghanistan’s foreign minister called on the U.S. to reopen its embassy and invest in the country — a near-impossible sell for now, analysts and former diplomats say.

items.title: Will Sudan’s El Obeid Become the Next El Fasher? What to Know.
items.summary: Taking El Obeid would allow the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces to consolidate its hold on western Sudan, a significant strategic goal.

items.title: With Trump’s Hamas Deal in Peril, Kushner Set to Visit Israel for Gaza Talks
items.summary: Jared Kushner, President Trump’s senior aide, is expected to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, who has rejected a U.S.-backed deal to disarm Hamas.

items.title: Kevin Rideout, American Missionary Kidnapped in Niger, Is Released
items.summary: Kevin Rideout, a pilot, was abducted from his home in the country’s capital, Niamey, last fall. His mission organization said he was in “good health” after his release.

items.title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, a novelty candidate, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

items.title: France’s Top Court Strikes Down Ban on Social Media for Children
items.summary: The move was a setback for President Emmanuel Macron, who championed the ban. He vowed to pass a new version before he leaves office next spring.

items.title: Record-Breaking Rainfall Leaves Eight Dead and Thousands Stranded in Japan
items.summary: Three months’ worth of rain fell in just 12 hours in a region east of Tokyo, leading to deadly flooding.

items.title: As Europe Gets Hotter, Its Transportation Systems Struggle to Cope
items.summary: The continent’s railways and roads “were engineered for a climate that no longer exists,” one expert said.

items.title: Outrage at UnitedHealth and Other Insurers Persists After Brian Thompson Killing
items.summary: Higher premiums and rising medical bills have intensified Americans’ dissatisfaction with their medical coverage.

items.title: Jeff Bezos Buys a Piece of Liverpool Football Club
items.summary: It is the first known investment by Mr. Bezos, one of the world’s richest men, into a sports team.

items.title: July Retail Sales Notch Biggest Drop in Over a Year
items.summary: The data for July showed the biggest drop in more than a year, as American households face the economic strains brought on by persistent inflation

items.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
items.summary: Investment gains at Alphabet and Amazon reveal a new way in which technology companies’ fortunes are increasingly linked.

items.title: Why Japan Is Struggling to Stop the Yen’s Decline
items.summary: The currency has resumed its slide, eroding gains after the U.S. Treasury intervened to prop it up, as concerns mount about the direction of the country’s spending.

items.title: The Markets Have Been on a Roll. Is It Time to Hedge Your Bets?
items.summary: The S&P 500 is in position for a rare fourth year of consecutive annual gains. Risks are rising, our columnist says, yet Wall Street is doubling down.

items.title: Robinhood Bets Again on a Public Venture Capital Fund
items.summary: The trading platform raised $200 million for a second publicly traded vehicle to let ordinary investors buy into privately held start-ups.

items.title: New Yorkers Can’t Stop Lining Up for This Sushi
items.summary: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on sushi and other items are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.

items.title: A Silicon Valley Dirt Farmer Hangs Up His Shears
items.summary: Andy Mariani grows exotic and ethereally delicious stone fruit in the shadow of tech giants. But at age 80, it’s time to give up the land.

items.title: How Pennsylvania Got Hooked on Games That Look a Lot Like Slot Machines
items.summary: A legal loophole kept “skill games” from being considered gambling. Now lawmakers are trying to save them from a court ruling.

items.title: I Tested a Popular A.I. Slop Detector. It Felt Empowering.
items.summary: Pangram excels at distinguishing chatbot-generated words from human writing. But it’s not reliable for spotting artificial images.

items.title: America Wants to Make Its Own Humanoid Robots. That Won’t Be Easy.
items.summary: China already manufactures humanoid robots by the thousands. A new generation of U.S. start-ups is betting that there is still time to compete.

items.title: Zuckerberg’s Anti-Doom Fantasy + Finally an A.I. Detector That Works + A.I. Math
items.summary: “The first rule of Mark Zuckerberg is never count out Mark Zuckerberg.”

items.title: Chatbots Are Pushing Us Toward a Post-Human Internet
items.summary: In matters of work, school and even romance, we turn to A.I. chatbots. But what happens when the bots begin talking to one another?

items.title: Judge Affirms Settlement Allowing HPE’s Deal for Juniper
items.summary: States had opposed an agreement allowing a Hewlett Packard Enterprise acquisition, calling the settlement ineffective and corrupt.

items.title: Another OpenAI Executive, Denise Dresser, Departs the A.I. Start-Up
items.summary: Denise Dresser, who was previously the C.E.O. of Slack, is the latest in a string of executives to leave the artificial intelligence start-up.

items.title: 3 Ex-Georgia Deputies Used Flock Cameras to Stalk People, Sheriff Says
items.summary: The former Bibb County deputies were arrested this week amid a growing national debate over Flock cameras, which can be found on roads in every state but Alaska.

items.title: Driver Sets Record for Hydrogen-Powered Vehicle at More Than 406 M.P.H.
items.summary: Andy Green, a 64-year-old retired Royal Air Force pilot from Britain, was already the only person to break the sound barrier on land. “The ground comes at you very, very quickly,” he said.

items.title: Thrive Holdings, A.I.-Focused Buyer of Service Firms, Raises $2 Billion
items.summary: The company, Thrive Holdings, acquires businesses to infuse them with artificial intelligence and drew interest from backers like SoftBank.
